## Natural history notes

A small slug moth characterized by its brown to tan wings with darker shading and a compact, rounded resting posture. In Florida, it is found in hardwood hammocks, forests, parks, yards, forest edges, and other wooded habitats where broadleaf host trees and shrubs occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the unusual slug-like caterpillars feed on leaves of trees such as oak, cherry, and related hardwoods, moving slowly across foliage and serving as prey for birds, spiders, wasps, and other insect-eating animals.
